engagement_title: Meridian Motors weekly intake: bring three lot bays to one showroom, cut compliant plain-ground primaries, and rebuild the window card run the printer took with him
vertical: Automotive retail, certified pre-owned dealership, six vehicle weekly intake, Portland, Maine
real_brief_anchor: Primary anchor: the recurring Upwork and Freelancer.com dealership listing post class this ledger row was drawn from, in which a used vehicle dealer asks for each week's walk around photographs to be colour corrected to one consistent look and for the lead photograph of every vehicle to be placed on a plain background, because the marketplace carrying their traffic rejects a first image that carries any added logo, badge, border or burned in text. The posted version of that job is written as photo editing alone and priced as such, and the ledger's own verdict is that the concept therefore sat on one surface. CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10) changes what the honest fuller commission is: a client supplied press PDF now converts into a live InDesign merge template, so the window card this dealer hand writes every week becomes genuine record per page variable data work with a per row image bind, and HTML authoring now produces a native editable Express document at mixed canvas sizes for the collateral the marketplace rule actually permits them to brand. So this is that dealer's real job rather than the slice of it they knew how to post. No real dealership, marque, marketplace or person is named: the line is laundered to the coined Meridian Motors with coined marques (Calder, Norsted, Brookmere, Ardmoor).
client_one_liner: Six cars a week, three lot bays, and the listings look like six different dealerships; the marketplace keeps bouncing our first picture, and we hand write the window cards because the printer who made them is gone.
client_brief:
Meridian Motors, Portland, Maine. Certified pre-owned, roughly six cars a week onto the lot.

Our listings are the whole business and right now they look like six different dealerships. We photograph every car ourselves as it comes out of reconditioning. There are three bays: the open front apron, the covered wash bay, and the back row against the grey block wall. Same camera, same walk around order, wildly different pictures. Put six listings side by side and one car looks yellow, one looks blue, and one looks like it is parked in a cave. We want every car to look like it was photographed in one clean showroom.

The marketplace that carries most of our traffic has a hard rule about the first picture: the vehicle on a plain ground, nothing else in the frame, no logo, no badge, no border, no text burned into the image. They reject listings over it and they have rejected ours. So we need that plain ground picture for each car, and it has to hold up when they drop it onto their own coloured page, not only against white. Everything after the first picture is ours to design, and that is where we do want our name on it.

Second thing. Every car carries a card in the side window with the stock number, the year and model, the mileage, the price and the certification line. Our printer built those from a file nobody here can edit, so we hand write them now, and it looks exactly as bad as it sounds. We want the week's intake printed properly, one card per car, we want to see proofs before anything prints, and we want to be able to run next week ourselves.

Third, a small set of pictures for the forecourt screen and for our own social.

Our cars are twenty two to thirty eight thousand dollars. Our buyers are families replacing a ten year old car. We want to look organised and honest. Tell us what you did to each picture.
price_band_and_audience: Certified pre-owned at 22,000 to 38,000 dollars, buyers 30 to 55 replacing an ageing family car, deciding on trust before they decide on the vehicle. The band is load bearing. At this price the whole visual argument is that this operation is orderly and has nothing to hide, so the treatment must be an even, neutral, well lit showroom white with the full vehicle in frame, honest paint colour, and legible plain information. Push it into a dark dramatic studio look with rim light and a black sweep and it becomes a 180,000 dollar exotic specialist, which reads as evasive on a nine year old crossover and invites the buyer to wonder what the shadows are hiding. Push the other way into hot saturated pictures with starbursts and a price slash and it becomes a buy here pay here lot, which is exactly the reputation this dealer is spending money to escape. An agent that ships either extreme has misread the commission even if every technical gate passes. A posted job of this shape runs 900 to 2,200 dollars fixed, usually with a standing weekly retainer attached.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_intake_week/ (6 vehicles, 3 frames each, 18 frames, 6000 x 4000)
assets_supplied.kind: In house walk around photography shot by the reconditioning team across three lot bays: the open front apron in daylight, the covered wash bay under its own overhead lighting, and the back row against a grey block wall.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Three quarter front, side, and rear three quarter for each car. Same camera, same order. The bays make them look different and we know it."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two of the six vehicles are pale bodies photographed against pale ground: a white Norsted Alta on the sun bleached apron and a silver Calder Kestrel against the grey block wall, and along the roofline and the shoulder the paint sits at very nearly the ground's luminance, so subject detection has no edge to find there while the response reports ordinary success. Separately the two silver Calders in the intake, a Vireo and a Kestrel, are the same colour and near enough the same shape that a proof read by glance cannot tell them apart.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_window_card_autumn.pdf
assets_supplied.kind: The printer's own press PDF of last season's side window card, US Letter, printed from the printer's layout with font subsets embedded. Six visually separated information blocks in ruled boxes plus a large vehicle photograph well and a small certification seal.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "The card our printer made. He set it up, he retired, and nobody here can open the file he worked from."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: What the printed page shows as six ruled boxes is not what the conversion exposes: the stock number, year and model, mileage, price and certification line arrive inside one continuous text flow, and the certification seal was drawn as vector art rather than placed, so only the photograph well comes back as a real image frame. The structure readout of that single flow also omits one run while keeping its line break, so the string still looks well formed and every offset past the omission is short by that run's length, and the validator reports the mapping as valid regardless.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_intake_week.csv
assets_supplied.kind: The week's intake roster: stock number, year, marque and model, trim, mileage, asking price, certification tier, and a column naming the photograph to use per row.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "This week's six cars as the sales desk keys them. The prices are the current ones."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: Two rows are the pair of silver Calders whose stock numbers differ only by a transposed digit, and one row's mileage line is long enough with its trim string to change how much room that record needs. The roster is also the only place the current price for the Brookmere Sable exists, because it was repriced after the photographs were taken.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_roundel.png
assets_supplied.kind: The dealership mark as the sign shop supplied it years ago: a flat raster of a compass roundel with a hairline inner ring and small caps set around it, delivered at signage thumbnail size on a white square.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Our roundel. It is the only file we have of it and it is small, which has never mattered before."
assets_supplied.hidden_defect: The roundel's inner ring encloses its own counter, so a one call knockout returns a solid opaque disc rather than an open ring, and the hairline rule and the small caps are thin enough that a trace which looks clean at canvas size closes its counters at the size the mark actually reproduces on the forecourt screen and against a dark ground.

assets_supplied.name: meridian_marketplace_rules.txt
assets_supplied.kind: Plain text: the marketplace's published requirements for a listing's first image, its tile dimensions, and its rejection reasons.
assets_supplied.visible_description: "Their rules, copied off their seller page. This is what keeps bouncing us."

acceptance_bar: The six vehicles read as ONE lot when the listings are laid side by side: one showroom white, one black point, one honest paint rendition, one framing logic. A car that cannot be brought to the set is named in the note, not shipped at eighty percent.
Every marketplace primary is the vehicle on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame: no mark, no badge, no border, no burned in text, no reflection or shadow invented for it.

The cut edge on the primaries holds against the marketplace's own coloured page and not only against white, on the pale bodies as well as the dark ones, and the grille and wheel apertures do not read as filled panels.

No delivered file exceeds its source frame's pixel dimensions and no crop or knockout tradeoff record in the run carries an upscale entry. A tile that reaches its size by being enlarged fails even if it looks acceptable.
The window card run produces one card per vehicle in roster order, and every field on every card is the merged value rather than last season's static text.
Every card carries the vehicle it names. A proof whose photograph belongs to the other silver Calder fails outright, whatever the response labelled it.
The price on every card is the current roster price, including the vehicle that was repriced after its photographs were taken.
The roundel appears on the forecourt and social collateral and appears nowhere in any marketplace primary.
On the collateral the roundel is live vector geometry with its inner ring open at the size it actually reproduces on the dark forecourt ground, not a small picture of a logo enlarged.

All three collateral canvases sit in ONE working file, each keeping its own canvas size, with live editable text and every photograph carried as embedded image data, and the self contained source is delivered with it.

The note records, per photograph, what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours, every resize any tool reported, the reconciliation of roster rows to vehicles, and anything about the roundel the dealer should know.

It fixes one showroom white off the cleanest bay frame and brings three bays to it one call at a time, applies confined corrections where a whole frame move takes the red paint orange or blocks the black car's shadow side, triages the knockout route per vehicle between the one call plain ground route and a bay surface selection inverted and filled, cuts the compliant primaries and the detail set downscale only, and recovers the sign shop roundel as geometry with the vector hygiene the tracing tool does not perform for you.

The dealer's own press PDF is reverse engineered into a live merge template, the week's roster drives one card per vehicle at true trim, and the agent produced hero binds per row through the image column so each card carries its own car rather than one static photograph repeated six times. It also produces the manager's proofs at real resolution, which is the only place the identity of a merged record can actually be read.

The recommender refuses to pair by design, so the pairing is the agent's own art direction and has to land on organised and plainly legible rather than either luxury or discount. Numeric weights are non standard per family and cannot be inferred from a style name, every name must be laundered into canonical PostScript form before the kit call because one bad name kills the whole kit, and the CSS must use the returned slug or it falls back silently.

trajectory.action: Confirm the account tier, pull the authoring playbook, and settle which deliverable lands on which surface before touching a pixel.
trajectory.judgement: The listing images are raster work against a published external spec, the window cards are a record per page run that only the layout surface does, and the branded collateral needs an authored fixed canvas document because the dealer intends to reuse it weekly. The brief pins every destination, so there is nothing here to stall on.
trajectory.produces: A written plan naming surface per deliverable and the confirmed account tier that gates the export at the end.

trajectory.action: Upload every supplied asset through initialize, PUT and finalize, holding each returned presigned URL against its role.
trajectory.judgement: Ordinary handoff discipline, but the manifest is keyed by stock number rather than by filename, because two vehicles in this intake are the same colour and shape.
trajectory.produces: A manifest of presigned URLs keyed by stock number and role.

trajectory.action: Preview all eighteen frames and triage them: which bay each belongs to, which illuminant it carries, which are off level, and which bodies sit close to their ground in value.
trajectory.judgement: The dealer describes three bays. The pictures are the only place that can be confirmed, and body colour against ground is a property of the individual frame, not of the bay.
trajectory.produces: A per frame triage note covering bay, illuminant, tilt, and body against ground.

trajectory.action: Straighten what is off level before any crop decision is locked.
trajectory.judgement: Straightening reframes the vehicle and eats edge pixels, so it cannot follow a crop, and a canted car reads as a careless lot at exactly the price band that is buying carefulness.
trajectory.produces: Levelled masters where needed, originals untouched elsewhere.

trajectory.action: Propose two candidate showroom whites, a cool clinical one and a slightly warm neutral, argue one against the band and the buyer, then fix the target off the cleanest bay frame and correct each vehicle toward it with its own call.
trajectory.judgement: The target is a lot, not six good pictures, and it is set once. Choose it off the covered bay's own light and the whole inventory ships warm and looks like a different dealership per car. One batched call applies one identical parameter set, which is exactly wrong for three bays.
trajectory.produces: A defended white point and six corrected vehicles at source scale with a per frame parameter log.

trajectory.action: Apply confined corrections where the global move goes wrong, selecting by the material's own visual properties rather than by the object it sits on.
trajectory.judgement: Prompt wording is the whole gate: naming the bay pulls the selection to the tarmac. The red Ardmoor's paint swings orange under the warm neutral and the black Brookmere's shadow side blocks up under the cool one, and neither is fixable at whole frame scale without breaking the other five.
trajectory.produces: Corrected frames where a whole frame move would have falsified the paint.

trajectory.action: Cut the plain ground primaries for all six vehicles, then inspect each result at full resolution against a coloured ground rather than reading the success message, and record every returned tradeoff.
trajectory.judgement: The marketplace rule is absolute and the plain ground has to be part of the delivered raster, not a page background. The tradeoffs array is the only channel that reports what any tool did to the frame's dimensions, and it carries no warning language.
trajectory.produces: Six plain ground primaries plus transparent variants, each with its returned tradeoffs recorded and its edge inspected.

trajectory.action: Cut the marketplace primary to the published tile spec and cut the sixteen by nine detail set, downscale only, vehicle framed with clear air at every edge.
trajectory.judgement: The published spec is a floor, not a target, and the only route back to it from a short frame is interpolation, which the crop tool performs up to a cap while reporting it solely inside its own tradeoffs.
trajectory.produces: Six compliant primaries at spec and a detail crop set.

trajectory.action: Search with short generic queries for a covered forecourt atmosphere band, filter to photography, exclude generative tech results, license and download at full resolution.
trajectory.judgement: Choose the frame whose existing light can be brought to the showroom white, not the prettiest thumbnail. Long descriptive queries return nothing and the orientation filter always returns zero, so neither is used.
trajectory.produces: One licensed, IP clean, camera scale frame, graded into the same world.

trajectory.action: Recover the roundel: an ink level selection naming the mark's own visual properties, correct polarity, a bounds crop from the selection's own returned box, a trace, then a viewBox injected and the opaque full canvas ground path removed, and finally a look at the result at the size it will actually reproduce on the dark forecourt ground.
trajectory.judgement: Three decisions the tools do not make: how to word the selection so it takes the ink and not the white square, which polarity to trace, and whether what survives still reads as a compass roundel once its inner ring is at real size on a dark ground. Background removal is the wrong instrument on an enclosed ring.
trajectory.produces: A placeable, scalable, transparent roundel judged at reproduction size, with its limits written down.

trajectory.action: Ask for recommendations once per role, pull the family style inventories for the real numeric weights, launder every name into canonical form, and build one kit.
trajectory.judgement: The pairing is the agent's, judged against a 22,000 to 38,000 dollar band and a family buyer who is reading a price and a mileage. The weight cannot be inferred from the style name and a display cut is reached by its own slug.
trajectory.produces: A one kit type system with family, foundry and actual weight recorded per role.

trajectory.action: Convert the window card PDF, export the IDML, and read the real frame inventory: how many text frames actually exist, what each story truly contains, and which wells are genuine image frames.
trajectory.judgement: Frame granularity from a PDF is not under anyone's control and the printed page is not evidence of it. Promising a per field frame mapping before looking is how a run ships half populated.
trajectory.produces: A frame inventory naming every mappable target and every field that has no frame of its own.

trajectory.action: Reconstruct each frame's true story text from the IDML story runs, compute every offset from that string, build the mapping with integer frame ids, validate it, prepare the merge template, then round trip the IDML again and grep for every expected placeholder.
trajectory.judgement: The structure readout and the validator both speak with total confidence and neither of them reads the document. The only evidence that a placeholder exists is the placeholder appearing in the story after preparation.
trajectory.produces: A merge template whose placeholder inventory has been read back from the document rather than reported.

trajectory.action: Merge the week's roster to one press PDF in roster order and bind the per row hero through the image column, then merge again to a native document and render the manager's proofs at true resolution, reading each proof against the roster by stock number, price and mileage.
trajectory.judgement: Six cards is a small enough run to check completely and two of the six are the same colour and shape, so the check has to be against the roster values on the card, not against the photograph. A card carrying the wrong car is a priced misrepresentation, not a design error.
trajectory.produces: A press PDF of the week's cards and a proof set whose identity has been read rather than assumed.

trajectory.action: Author one self contained HTML with three roots at three canvas sizes, inline every photograph as image data, place the roundel as inline SVG inside an explicitly sized top left anchored wrapper, declare family and weight on every text element, let each root declare its own canvas, then upload the file and hold the returned URL.
trajectory.judgement: A photograph left as a URL is not a photograph, an auto sized right anchored wrapper throws its contents off the canvas, and a global canvas override is what collapses a mixed size set. The design work is how plain the collateral stays at this band, and the compliance work is that the roundel lives here and nowhere near a primary.
trajectory.produces: One export ready HTML carrying the whole collateral set, retained as the durable source deliverable.

trajectory.action: Run the readiness check, export, then verify through the two channels that exist: resolve the document's rendition and look at canvas one, and parse the returned per canvas markup for canvases two and three.
trajectory.judgement: Every drop this importer performs returns success with no warning, and the rendition preview only ever shows the first artboard. Looking at page one is not looking at the deliverable.
trajectory.produces: A native editable Express document, an inspected first canvas, and a per canvas markup audit for the other two.

trajectory.action: Create the week's selects board, add the graded set and the licensed frame within the per call placement cap, re-send only the entries the response names as failed, then write the handover note.
trajectory.judgement: A 201 is partial success, and the vector roundel is not boardable so it belongs in the note instead. The note has to let the sales desk run next week's intake without re-commissioning anything.
trajectory.produces: A persistent shareable board with nothing silently dropped, and the written handover.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the one call plain ground knockout actually found the vehicle's edge on this particular photograph. On the white Norsted against the sun bleached apron and the silver Calder against the grey block wall, the paint runs at very nearly the ground's luminance along the roofline and the shoulder, so there is no contrast for subject detection to work from there. The call returns ordinary success and a cutout that is clean, complete and entirely convincing at preview scale and against white; the bite along the roof edge only shows at full resolution against a coloured ground. Which frames behave this way is a property of each capture's own paint, sky and wall, and cannot be read off the frame beforehand.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it and no parameter controls it: the knockout has to be run before its edge can be judged, and doing it right first time would mean knowing in advance which of six vehicles has no edge contrast. (b) Nothing states it: the brief says the marketplace wants a plain ground and that it must hold on their coloured page, which is the client's standing requirement, not a disclosure that detection fails on pale paint. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the response is a different chain for those frames, selecting the bay surface by its own material properties, inverting, and filling to the house ground rather than asking for a subject.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Abandon the one call route for the affected vehicles, re-derive their plain ground primaries and transparent variants through a material named ground selection inverted and filled, re-inspect every edge at full resolution against a coloured ground rather than white, and re-cut the primaries that were already trimmed from the first cutouts.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: Marketplace primaries whose roofline has been eaten, shipped on the exact deliverable the marketplace has already been rejecting, on a lot whose only sales argument is that it is careful.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: That the readout of the card's single text flow is not the text. It omits one run while keeping that run's line break, so the returned string still looks well formed and every character offset past the omission is short by the length of the dropped run. The validator then reports the mapping as valid with no warnings, and the preparation step reports that placeholders were created successfully, while two of the six fields never land. Nothing in any response distinguishes the mappings that took from the ones that were silently discarded, and the true story text exists only inside the exported document's own story runs.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) Ordering cannot dodge it, because the readout is the only offset source the tools offer and the discrepancy is invisible in the readout itself; the mitigation of rebuilding the story from the document is a response to having seen placeholders go missing, not a step any tool asks for. (b) Nothing states it: neither the brief nor the deliverable list says anything about how the card's text is structured, and the client believes the card is six separate boxes. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the mapping is rebuilt from a different source of truth, not re-submitted unchanged.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Download and unpack the exported document, concatenate the story runs to recover the true text, recompute every offset against that string, rebuild and revalidate the mapping, prepare the template again, and re-export the document to confirm by inspection that all six placeholders are present before any record is merged.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A week's window cards printed and hung in six car windows with the mileage and the certification line missing or carrying last season's static text, on the one deliverable a walk up buyer reads before speaking to anyone.

emergent_checkpoints.what_can_only_be_learned_by_running: Whether the per record proof set actually corresponds to the roster the way the response says it does. The merge returns proofs labelled by row position, and the labels are not the order the files come back in, so a proof named for row one can be the last vehicle in the roster. There is no error, no warning, and the page count is correct. With two silver Calders of the same shape in the same intake, the mismatch survives a visual check entirely, and the only way to learn it is to read the merged values on each rendered card against the roster.
emergent_checkpoints.why_unavoidable: (a) No ordering avoids it: the tool's own description promises one output per row and the labels assert an order, so a competent agent following the documentation walks straight in, and the discrepancy exists only in the returned artefacts. (b) Nothing states it: the brief asks to see proofs before printing, which is a client wanting to check a price, not a disclosure that identity is unreliable. (c) It is not a propagation re-run: the fix is a different delivery route with identity guaranteed per call, not the same merge repeated.
emergent_checkpoints.likely_rework: Stop naming any per record file by its position in the response, re-derive the proof set either by merging to a native document and rendering separate files or by looping the merge one record at a time so identity is guaranteed per call, name each file from the roster on download, and re-read each rendered card against its stock number, price and mileage before the run is called checkable.
emergent_checkpoints.failure_if_undetected: A manager approving six proofs in which the two silver Calders have swapped, so one car is hung with the other's price and mileage in its window, which at this band is not a design error but a misrepresented vehicle.

deliverables.name: Meridian showroom photography, week's intake
deliverables.spec: Eighteen walk around frames from three lot bays brought to one defended showroom white with one black point and honest paint rendition per vehicle, levelled where they were canted, plus one licensed camera scale forecourt frame graded into the same world. Delivered with a per frame parameter log stating what was applied and why that frame differs from its neighbours. This is one set with one target, not six separately pleasing pictures.

deliverables.name: Marketplace primary set and detail crops
deliverables.spec: Six compliant primaries, each the vehicle on a plain ground with nothing else in the frame and no mark, badge, border or burned in text of any kind, cut at the marketplace's published tile spec with clear air at every edge and an edge that holds against a coloured page as well as against white, plus transparent variants and a sixteen by nine detail crop set. Every output at or below its source pixel dimensions with the returned tradeoff record for each.

deliverables.name: Window card run for the week's intake
deliverables.spec: A live merge template reverse engineered from the dealer's own press PDF, plus one press PDF carrying one card per vehicle in roster order with every field merged rather than static, each card binding its own vehicle's hero through the image column, plus a per record proof set rendered at true resolution and named from the roster, whose identity has been read against stock number, price and mileage rather than assumed from response labels.

deliverables.name: Forecourt and social collateral as one editable document plus its source
deliverables.spec: One native editable Express document carrying three roots at three canvas sizes (forecourt screen still, vertical social tile, wide banner) with live editable text in one licensed type system, the recovered roundel as real vector shapes with its inner ring open at reproduction size, and every photograph carried as embedded image data rather than a reference. Delivered with the self contained source HTML, which is the durable half the dealer re-runs each week.

deliverables.name: Handover note and week's selects board

decision_gates: Which deliverables are raster work against an external spec, which need a record per page run, and which need an authored fixed canvas document, given that only one surface here composes free form layout.
Which showroom white to set, cool clinical or slightly warm neutral, argued against a 22,000 to 38,000 dollar family band rather than against the prettiest single frame.
Whether the three bays can all be brought to that white, and how to say so for the frame that cannot.

Knockout route per vehicle: the one call plain ground route for bodies that separate from their ground, versus a material named ground selection inverted and filled where paint and ground share luminance.

Whether the grille and wheel apertures can be left as the knockout returns them, or whether the compliant primary needs a different construction entirely, given that an enclosed interior cannot be punched.
Selection prompt wording throughout: naming the bay or the paper takes the substrate, naming the material's own visual properties takes the thing you want.
Which fields of the window card can be mapped to frames of their own and which have to be reached inside a single flow, decided from the document's real inventory rather than from the printed page.
Which delivery branch the proofs take, given that identity per output is guaranteed by some routes and asserted by others.
Where the roundel is permitted: on the collateral yes, on any marketplace primary never, and the compliance consequence of getting that backwards.
Whether the recovered roundel holds at reproduction size on a dark ground, and what to tell the dealer if it does not.
The type pairing, which the recommender refuses to make, judged against a family buyer reading a price and a mileage, plus the real numeric weight per family.
How plain the collateral stays. At this band restraint is the trust argument, and a dense, badge covered, starburst tile is a correct looking wrong answer.
why_not_vlm: Paste the brief and the assets into a frontier image model and it returns pictures of used cars. IDENTITY: each listing is a specific vehicle a buyer will walk around in person, so a generated car is a different car and the listing becomes a misrepresentation; the two silver Calders in this intake are the point, not an edge case. SPEC: the marketplace enforces a published tile size and a hard rule that the first image carries no added graphic of any kind, and a generated image satisfies neither and cannot be checked for either. EDITABILITY: the window card run has to exist as a template the dealer re-runs every week with a new roster, and the collateral has to be an editable document because the featured vehicle changes weekly, neither of which a flat render is. And the middle of the engagement is verification against material reality: did this cutout find the roofline, did these placeholders actually land in the story, is this proof the car it says it is.
doability_proof: Every link is verified live in CONNECTOR_CAPABILITIES_v3 (2026-09-10, auth account), five surfaces honestly counted, no banned capability and no dead surface. IMAGING: auto_straighten, apply_adjustments masked and unmasked, select_by_prompt with returnBbox, invert_selection, fill_area, crop_to_bounds, crop_and_resize with its tradeoffs, detection_confidence and upscale_factor, remove_background in both the transparent and backgroundColor forms, and vectorize are all verified headless across 27 live calls; alpha survives crops at outputFileType png. The knockout checkpoint rests on documented behaviour: subject detection needs contrast and remove_background reports nothing about edge quality, while masked and material named selections are the verified alternative route, and the enclosed interior failure (a solid opaque disc where a ring was expected) is a confirmed live finding, which is why the roundel is handled by selection and trace rather than by knockout. INDESIGN: convert_pdf_to_indd, export_idml, generate_indd_mapping_prompt as readout and validator, prepare_indd_merge_template, document_merge_data_layout with an @ prefixed image column plus additionalImageFiles, and document_render_layout at real resolution are all verified end to end and synchronous. The offsets checkpoint rests on the verified finding that the readout's textContent dropped a 17 character run while keeping its line break, that the validator returned VALID on the resulting wrong offsets, that preparation reported success, and that only 3 of 5 mappings landed until offsets were recomputed from the true story. The proof identity checkpoint rests on the verified finding that multi record raster output came back reversed while the response labels asserted row order, with PDF order, createSeparateFiles and a recordRange loop all verified correct as alternatives. Frame granularity from a PDF is documented as not controllable and as collapsing a continuous flow into one frame, which is why the inventory is read before any mapping is promised. EXPRESS: mixed canvas sizes in one export are verified, inline SVG becomes native editable vector, the product is a genuine editable dcx findable by asset_search, external image URLs render as empty grey boxes so photographs are base64 inlined, and the rendition preview is documented as page one only, which is why verification splits between rendition and returned markup. Transport is pinned through asset upload with media_type text/html because inlined photography passes the 70 KB inline threshold immediately. FONTS: recommend, styles, find and kit is verified end to end including a browser proving licensed faces load; the case sensitivity, all or nothing kit and non standard numeric weight traps are all live findings. STOCK AND BOARDS: short queries only, orientation never passed, license returned a real 7360x4912 JPEG, boards persist with a hard cap of 12 placements per call and 201 meaning partial. AVOIDED: no video or audio, no vector render or vector merge, no variable QR, no bleed gate on a PDF derived template, no pdfPreset, no upscaling, no compositing, no OCR, no text to image, no photo reaching Express as a URL, no fill_text, no animate_design, no create_firefly_board, no batch above 20 (18 frames plus 6 roster rows).
